target_customer: Doctors and clinics in India who keep paper patient records
problem: Indian doctors lack simple tools to digitize patient records, and prior EMR products saw low adoption.
business_model: iPad based electronic medical records app for doctors, pricing not stated by any source

founders.name: Chaitu Aluru
previous_startups: Speechify Chrome extension, Kindle integration and API (project)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists his past projects and calls himself a builder. Inc42 2017 names Krishna Chaitanya Aluru as DocTalk co-founder and CTO; that this is the same person is likely but not stated on the YC page.

founders.name: Vamsee Chamakura
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; Inc42 names him a DocTalk co-founder. No background given.

founders.name: Akshat Goenka
founders.background_notes: Inc42 2017 calls him founder and CEO of DocTalk. He is not on the Pulse YC page, so the link is inferred.

competitors.name: Doxper
competitors.what: Digital pen and paper system that digitizes prescriptions and records for Indian doctors
competitors.traction_then: About 300 doctors onboard at an annual subscription of Rs 15,000, per May 2017 coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: An iPad EMR with records, sync and doctor workflows is standard app engineering, with some difficulty in handwriting and vernacular input and clinic connectivity in India.

defensibility.rationale: EMR features were copyable by rivals such as Practo and Healthplix; record lock in could add switching costs once doctors adopt, but no source shows it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source says what incumbents did to Pulse specifically.

market_need_then: Indian coverage in 2016 and 2017 describes poor healthcare records and low EMR use among doctors. No Pulse specific demand data was found.

brand_strength.rationale: The Pulse name is shared with many health products, and the company appears under the DocTalk name in press.

outcome_analysis: Pulse joined YC in Winter 2017 as an iPad EMR for Indian doctors, and press on the same team under the name DocTalk reports a 5M first institutional round in November 2017 led by Khosla Ventures and Matrix Partners India. The YC directory marks the Pulse listing inactive, but no shutdown report or later history was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty. Whether DocTalk continued under another form is unknown.
notes: The YC page gives no website. That the YC Pulse listing is the DocTalk company is inferred from Inc42 (DocTalk in the W17 batch with Vamsee Chamakura and Chaitanya Aluru) and Aluru's YC page listing DocTalk Pulse EMR; this is not stated directly. A 2025 company named Pulse raising 4M for medical equipment is unrelated. The 120000 YC amount is stated in Inc42 as 7 percent equity. The 2017 5M round is labeled first institutional round by Inc42, so stage is other. Only one dated competitor source found; Practo and Healthplix were seen only in undated or later items.
